question: filter(pk__in=[]) returns an empty queryset without touching the database, filter(Q(pk__in=[]) | Q(name='x')) just drops the impossible branch from the OR, and exclude(pk__in=[]) returns everything. question: Several parts of Django add request-header names to the response header that tells shared proxies which incoming headers a page's body depends on; they all go through one shared helper that merges the new names with the existing ones case-insensitively and lets '*' override everything. Which code calls that shared helper? List every caller.
expected: patch_vary_headers (django/utils/cache.py) is called by SessionMiddleware.process_response (Cookie, when the session was accessed or deleted), CsrfViewMiddleware._set_token (Cookie, when the token cookie is set), GZipMiddleware.process_response (Accept-Encoding), LocaleMiddleware.process_response (Accept-Language), and the view decorators vary_on_cookie and vary_on_headers via their inner_func wrappers.
note: grep patch_vary_headers: 7 call sites in 6 functions (sessions middleware calls it twice); matches b11_truth callers.

question: Rendering a form with the anti-forgery hidden input, or decorating a view so it always hands out the anti-forgery cookie, both end up calling the one public function that returns the masked per-visitor token (creating the secret if there is none yet and flagging that the token cookie must go out with the reply). Which code calls that public function directly?
expected: django/middleware/csrf.py::get_token is called by csrf_input (the hidden <input> HTML used by Jinja2/dummy backends), by the nested _get_val of the csrf context processor (lazy csrf_token for Django templates), and by _EnsureCsrfCookie.process_view (behind @ensure_csrf_cookie).
note: grep 'get_token(' over django/: exactly these 3 (others are CsrfViewMiddleware._get_token). backends/utils.py also wraps it with lazy(get_token, str) at module level; that is a reference, not a call.

question: With APPEND_SLASH on, a request for /blog/post is redirected to /blog/post/ only if the original path does not resolve, the slashed path does resolve, and the view that would be hit has not opted out with the no_append_slash decorator. Where is that yes/no decision made?
expected: CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash checks settings.APPEND_SLASH and that path_info lacks a trailing slash, then uses is_valid_path on the original and slashed paths and reads the matched view's should_append_slash attribute. process_request/process_response call it and build the target with get_full_path_with_slash.

question: For a query string like ?color=red&color=blue, request.GET['color'] gives 'blue' rather than a list, and a key present with an empty value list gives [] instead of an error. Where is this lookup behaviour implemented?
expected: QueryDict subclasses MultiValueDict; MultiValueDict.__getitem__ fetches the stored list, raises MultiValueDictKeyError if the key is missing, returns list_[-1] (the last value) and [] when the list is empty.

question: When I assign a generator of str and bytes chunks as the body of a regular (non-streaming) HTTP reply object, Django consumes it immediately, encodes each chunk with the reply's charset, joins them into one bytestring and closes the generator if it can. Where does that assignment-time conversion happen?
expected: The HttpResponse.content property setter: for non-bytes/str iterables it joins make_bytes(chunk) for each chunk and calls value.close() if present, otherwise make_bytes(value); the result is stored as the single-element _container list.

question: A page includes a sub-template once per row of a 500-row table. Django loads and parses that sub-template only once per page rendering, accepts a name, a list of candidate names (the first that exists wins) or an already-built template object, and with the 'only' option gives it a fresh context holding just the extra values passed in. Where is all of this handled?
expected: IncludeNode.render in template/loader_tags.py resolves the template expression, uses an object with a render method directly, otherwise caches select_template(names) per node in context.render_context, resolves the extra values, and renders with context.new(values) when isolated ('only') or inside context.push(**values) otherwise.
note: Replaces a question whose answer is the only gzip module.

question: My custom path converter's to_python raises ValueError for malformed input. Instead of a 500, Django just treats that URL entry as not applicable and moves on (ending in a 404 if nothing else fits). Where is the ValueError swallowed?
expected: RoutePattern.match runs the compiled regex, then calls each converter's to_python on the captured kwargs; a ValueError makes it return None, so URLResolver.resolve treats the pattern as non-matching and keeps trying.

question: In the admin changelist, when I sort by a non-unique column such as 'last name', Django adds '-pk' at the end of ORDER BY so pagination is stable. It does not add it when the sort already contains a unique non-null column, or all columns of a unique_together / total unique constraint without nullable columns. Where is this decided?
expected: ChangeList._get_deterministic_ordering scans the ordering parts (str/F/OrderBy), stops if one is pk or a unique non-null field, otherwise checks unique_together and total_unique_constraints (skipping ones with nullable fields) and appends '-pk' if none is covered. ChangeList.get_ordering builds the ordering and calls it.
note: Many ordering-related methods in admin (get_ordering, get_ordering_field, get_ordering_field_columns, _get_default_ordering, ModelAdmin.get_ordering); only _get_deterministic_ordering appends -pk.

question: My ModelForm's Meta lists only ['title']; the view sets the model's unique 'slug' afterwards and saves. Duplicate slugs never produce a form error, and I get an IntegrityError at save time instead. Also, a form field I made optional is left blank while the underlying column is NOT NULL without blank=True, and the form reports nothing. Where does Django decide which model fields are left out of the model-level validation and uniqueness checks run by the form?
expected: BaseModelForm._get_validation_exclusions excludes model fields not on the form, fields outside Meta.fields / in Meta.exclude, fields that already failed form validation, and empty non-required form fields whose model field has blank=False. _post_clean passes this exclude list to instance.full_clean and validate_unique passes it to instance.validate_unique, so the unique slug is never checked.

question: In the admin, a changelist URL like ?author__publisher__country=FR fails with a 400 response (a suspicious-operation error saying filtering by that key isn't permitted), while ?title=x and ?author=3 work fine and ?author__publisher__country=FR starts working once I add that path to list_filter. Where is the rule that rejects the multi-relation query-string filter?
expected: BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed allows limit_choices_to lookups from raw-id popups, walks the lookup parts collecting relation hops (skipping hops whose target is already on the local FK), allows it if at most one relation part, and otherwise requires the joined path (or a prefix) to be in list_filter / date_hierarchy / SimpleListFilter parameter names. ChangeList.get_filters calls it for every query param and raises DisallowedModelAdminLookup when it returns False.

question: When I type `./manage.py migrate` in a terminal, Django first validates the project with the system checks framework before the command's handler runs (unless --skip-checks is passed). Trace the call path from the manage.py entry function to the point where all registered system checks are run. Also say where invoking the same command programmatically from Python turns this step off by default.
expected: execute_from_command_line -> ManagementUtility.execute (fetch_command(subcommand).run_from_argv) -> BaseCommand.run_from_argv (parse args) -> BaseCommand.execute (if requires_system_checks and not skip_checks) -> BaseCommand.check -> checks.run_checks i.e. CheckRegistry.run_checks. call_command sets defaults['skip_checks'] = True when not passed.

question: After I edit an object in the admin and press Save, its History page shows an entry like 'Changed title and price.' plus lines for inline objects that were added or deleted. Trace the path from the admin's edit-page entry point to the code that computes the labels of the changed fields for that history entry.
expected: ModelAdmin.change_view -> changeform_view (inside transaction.atomic) -> _changeform_view (after save_model/save_related) -> ModelAdmin.construct_change_message -> admin/utils.construct_change_message (builds JSON with added/changed/deleted, translations off) -> _get_changed_field_labels_from_form (verbose labels of form.changed_data); then log_change stores the LogEntry.

question: A user opens the 'reset your password' link from the email. If they already used it, or logged in after it was sent, or changed their e-mail address, the link is rejected as invalid. Trace the path from the view that handles the link to the code that mixes that per-user state into the signed value being compared.
expected: PasswordResetConfirmView.dispatch (get_user from uidb64, then token_generator.check_token for the URL token or the session token) -> PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token (parse ts_b36, recompute and constant_time_compare, check timeout) -> _make_token_with_timestamp (salted_hmac) -> _make_hash_value (pk + password hash + last_login + timestamp + email).

question: If I change how a single form joins its prefix and a field name into the HTML input name (e.g. 'author-name'), which code calls that per-form helper directly? Count only the form-level helper, not the formset's own helper that numbers each child form.
expected: BaseForm.add_prefix is called by BaseForm._clean_fields, add_initial_prefix, changed_data, BoundField.__init__ (html_name), construct_instance (value_omitted_from_data check), BaseInlineFormSet._construct_form (clearing pk/fk data on save_as_new) and BaseFormSet.full_clean (management_form.add_prefix in the missing-management-data error). BaseModelFormSet._construct_form and BaseFormSet._construct_form/empty_form call BaseFormSet.add_prefix, a different method.
note: SCIP only has the 3 BaseForm self-calls; the other 4 are calls on untyped receivers (bf: form param in BoundField.__init__ and construct_instance, form returned by super()._construct_form, self.management_form) verified by reading forms/models.py:54, :938/:940, boundfield.py:21, formsets.py:347. Distractors: models.py:607, formsets.py:173/:211 are BaseFormSet.add_prefix; db/models/query.py:1637 is Prefetch.add_prefix.

question: If I change the content-types manager method that returns (and caches, creating if missing) the content-type row for a given model class or instance, which code in Django calls it directly?
expected: ContentTypeManager.get_for_model is called by admin get_content_type_for_model (LogEntry/permissions), auth create_permissions (post_migrate), GenericForeignKey.get_forward_related_filter and get_content_type, GenericRelation.get_content_type and bulk_related_objects, and BaseGenericInlineFormSet.__init__ and save_new. The auth migration 0011 update_proxy_model_permissions also calls it on the historical manager.
note: SCIP has 6; grep found 2 more via ContentType.objects.db_manager(...).get_for_model (fields.py:164 in GenericForeignKey.get_content_type, fields.py:481 in GenericRelation.bulk_related_objects). Migration 0011 calls it on apps.get_model's manager (historical ContentTypeManager, use_in_migrations) -> accept only.

question: After I connected a receiver to the pre-removal signal of my Comment model, removing a single Post became much slower: Django now SELECTs every comment of the post with all its columns, sends the signal per comment and removes them in batches. Before, it issued a single DELETE ... WHERE post_id IN (...) without loading anything. Where is the logic that makes this choice, and what else (besides receivers) disables the fast path?
expected: Collector.collect asks Collector.can_fast_delete(related_model, from_field=field) for each reverse relation; can_fast_delete returns False when the model has pre/post_delete or m2m_changed receivers (_has_signal_listeners), when the relation's on_delete is not CASCADE, when the model has concrete parents other than the from_field link, when its own reverse relations are not all DO_NOTHING, or when it has generic relations. Without fast delete collect fetches sub_objs via related_objects and only defers non-key columns when there are no signal receivers.
note: Read deletion.py can_fast_delete and collect (only(*referenced_fields) branch).

question: One of my columns was declared with default=timezone.now() (with parentheses). Every time I run the command that generates migrations it writes yet another migration that alters this column, although I changed nothing in the model. Which code decides that the column definition has changed, and how does it compare old and new?
expected: MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields compares deep_deconstruct(old_field) with deep_deconstruct(new_field) for every field present in both states and emits an AlterField when they differ; deep_deconstruct recursively expands Field.deconstruct() kwargs, so a default evaluated at import time (a fresh datetime each run) never compares equal to the one frozen in the last migration.
note: Read autodetector.py generate_altered_fields / deep_deconstruct.

question: With multi-table inheritance, when I write a new child instance to the database Django first writes the row of each parent table (recursively, grandparents first), copies the parent's primary key into the child's link column, and only then writes the child's own row. Trace the calls from the instance's public persistence method to the code that writes each single table's row.
expected: Model.save calls Model.save_base, which (for non-raw saves) calls Model._save_parents; _save_parents recurses over meta.parents, calls Model._save_table(cls=parent) for each parent and sets the child's link attname from the parent pk; save_base then calls _save_table for the child's own table, which does _do_update/_do_insert.
note: All chain edges are in SCIP.

question: When I run the management command that applies pending migrations with --fake-initial, an initial migration whose tables and columns already exist is recorded as applied without running its operations. Trace the calls from the command to the code that inspects the existing tables and columns to make that call.
expected: migrate's Command.handle calls MigrationExecutor.migrate, which calls _migrate_all_forwards for a forwards plan; that calls apply_migration per migration, which with fake_initial calls detect_soft_applied; detect_soft_applied checks introspection.table_names and get_table_description for every CreateModel/AddField of an initial migration, and if all exist apply_migration sets fake=True and only record_migration runs.
note: All chain edges are in SCIP.

question: I rename a field on a model and run the command that writes new migration files. Django asks 'Did you rename ... to ...?' only when the old and new field definitions are identical apart from the name (or when the new one keeps the old column name through db_column). Trace the calls from the command to the place where that question is asked, and say where the comparison is made.
expected: makemigrations Command.handle builds a MigrationAutodetector and calls changes(), which calls _detect_changes; that calls generate_renamed_fields, which compares deep_deconstruct of each added field with each removed field of the same model (also allowing db_column == old column) and on a match calls self.questioner.ask_rename (InteractiveMigrationQuestioner.ask_rename prompts the user), then adds a RenameField operation.
note: SCIP resolves self.questioner.ask_rename to the base MigrationQuestioner.ask_rename; at runtime makemigrations passes InteractiveMigrationQuestioner.

question: If I change how the DDL layer builds generated names for indexes and constraints (table and column names joined, an 8-character hash suffix, truncation to the backend's maximum identifier length, no leading underscore or digit), which code calls that name builder directly?
expected: BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor._create_index_name is called directly by BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor._alter_field (the _check constraint name), _create_primary_key_sql (_pk), the nested name factories create_index_name (in _create_index_sql), create_fk_name (in _fk_constraint_name) and create_unique_name (in _create_unique_sql), and by the PostgreSQL DatabaseSchemaEditor._alter_field (the _like index).
note: grep '_create_index_name(' = 7 call sites in these 6 functions (postgresql twice); the nested factories are keyed as BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.create_*_name, their enclosing methods are in accept.

question: In the in-memory project representation that the migration framework builds, there is a method that, after one model's definition has been modified, re-renders that model and every model related to it (optionally delaying the related ones). If I change its signature, which code calls it directly?
expected: ProjectState.reload_model is called by ProjectState.add_model and by the state_forwards of AddField, RemoveField, AlterField, RenameField (operations/fields.py) and RenameModel, AlterModelTable, AlterTogetherOptionOperation (covers AlterUniqueTogether/AlterIndexTogether), AlterOrderWithRespectTo, AlterModelOptions, AlterModelManagers, AddIndex, RemoveIndex, AddConstraint, RemoveConstraint (operations/models.py). CreateModel/DeleteModel use add_model/remove_model; RenameModel also calls reload_models.
note: grep 'reload_model(' over django/ = 15 calling functions; SCIP only has AlterField.state_forwards and add_model because the state parameter is untyped.

question: When migrations are squashed (or a freshly generated migration is optimized), a step that creates a table followed by steps that add a column to it, change its options or unique_together, or rename it, is folded into the single creation step, and a creation followed by dropping the same table disappears completely. Where is the rule that folds a following operation into the creation step?
expected: CreateModel.reduce returns [] for a following DeleteModel of the same (non-proxy) model, and a new CreateModel with merged fields/options for RenameModel, AlterModelOptions, AlterTogetherOptionOperation, AlterOrderWithRespectTo and Add/Alter/Remove/RenameField on that model. MigrationOptimizer.optimize_inner calls operation.reduce pairwise.
note: Many reduce overloads across operations/*; the creation-specific one is CreateModel.reduce.

question: When a concrete model class inherits from another concrete model, Django automatically adds a one-to-one link to the parent named '<parent>_ptr' (unless the class already declares a one-to-one with parent_link=True), and that link ends up as the child's primary key. Where is the link field created, and where is it promoted to be the primary key?
expected: The metaclass ModelBase.__new__ collects declared parent links and, for each concrete parent without one, creates OneToOneField(base, on_delete=CASCADE, name='%s_ptr', auto_created=True, parent_link=True) and records it in new_class._meta.parents; Options._prepare, when no pk was set, promotes the first parent link (field.primary_key = True) via setup_pk.
note: base.py ~194-260 and options.py _prepare ~271-283.

question: filter(author__name='x') produces an INNER JOIN to the author table, but filter(Q(author__name='x') | Q(editor__name='y')) produces LEFT OUTER JOINs, and adding '& Q(author__age__gte=0)' turns the author JOIN back into INNER. Where is the per-table decision made, based on how many children of an AND/OR node required each table?
expected: JoinPromoter.update_join_types: for each table counted by add_votes, effective connector OR with votes < num_children -> promote to LOUTER; AND, or OR with votes == num_children -> demote to INNER; then calls Query.promote_joins / Query.demote_joins. It is run from Query._add_q per Q node and from Query.combine for qs1 | qs2.

question: annotate(total=F('price') * F('quantity')) works with price a DecimalField and quantity an IntegerField, but annotate(total=F('price') + F('discount')) with discount a FloatField raises FieldError 'mixed types: DecimalField, FloatField. You must set output_field'. Where is it decided which field-type pairs are acceptable for arithmetic and when the error is raised?
expected: CombinedExpression._resolve_output_field first tries BaseExpression._resolve_output_field (all sources same class, else FieldError 'mixed types'); on FieldError it looks up _resolve_combined_type(connector, lhs type, rhs type) in the _connector_combinators table (Integer/Integer, Integer/Decimal, Decimal/Integer, Integer/Float, Float/Integer for + - * /) and re-raises if no pair matches, so Decimal+Float fails.

question: Blog.objects.filter(entry__headline__contains='x', entry__pub_date__year=2008) uses a single JOIN to the entry table (both conditions on the same entry), but .filter(entry__headline__contains='x').filter(entry__pub_date__year=2008) adds a second JOIN to the entry table and matches blogs where different entries satisfy each condition. For a forward foreign key the second filter call reuses the existing JOIN. Where is this reuse behaviour decided?
expected: Query.add_q passes self.used_aliases as can_reuse; Query.setup_joins passes reuse=can_reuse only when the join is m2m/multi-valued (reverse FK, m2m), else None (always reusable); Query.join reuses an existing equal alias only if it is in that reuse set. Query.chain (called for every new queryset clone) resets used_aliases to an empty set unless filter_is_sticky, so a second filter() call cannot reuse the multi-valued join and creates a new alias.

question: Book.objects.values('author').annotate(n=Count('id')).order_by('title') returns one row per (author, title) instead of one per author: the title column silently ends up in the GROUP BY. Where is the ordering term added to the grouping?
expected: SQLCompiler.get_group_by starts from query.group_by (set by values()+annotate), then adds get_group_by_cols() of every select expression, of every order_by expression that is not a reference to a select alias, and of HAVING, then collapse_group_by and de-duplication. The order_by('title') expression is not a Ref, so title is added.

question: Negated filtering over a reverse foreign key, Author.objects.<the opposite of filter()>(book__title='x'), doesn't add a JOIN: it puts a NOT EXISTS (correlated sub-select over books) in the WHERE. Trace the calls from that public queryset method to the method that builds that inner sub-select.
expected: QuerySet.exclude -> QuerySet._filter_or_exclude -> QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace (adds ~Q) -> Query.add_q -> Query._add_q -> Query.build_filter, which calls setup_joins with allow_many=False for a negated branch; the multi-valued hop raises MultiJoin and build_filter calls Query.split_exclude, which builds an inner Query, trims leading joins, correlates with ResolvedOuterRef and wraps it in Exists.

question: I do Author.objects.prefetch_related('books') and loop over the result. Trace the calls from starting the loop to the code that hands each author its own pre-filled list of books, so author.books.all() does not hit the database again.
expected: QuerySet.__iter__ -> QuerySet._fetch_all (fills _result_cache, then since _prefetch_related_lookups and not _prefetch_done) -> QuerySet._prefetch_related_objects -> prefetch_related_objects (walks each lookup level, get_prefetcher) -> prefetch_one_level, which runs the prefetcher's get_prefetch_queryset, buckets related objects by key and stores a queryset with _result_cache set into obj._prefetched_objects_cache[cache_name] (or to_attr / field cache).

question: Asking a sliced or .distinct() queryset (or one that already has annotations) for its number of rows produces SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT ...) subquery instead of a plain COUNT. Trace from the public queryset method that returns the row total to the code that decides to wrap the original SQL in a subquery.
expected: QuerySet.count (returns len(_result_cache) if cached) -> Query.get_count (clones, adds Count('*') as summary annotation '__count') -> Query.get_aggregation, which uses a subquery (AggregateQuery wrapping the inner query) when group_by is a tuple, the query is sliced, has existing annotations, is distinct or has a combinator; otherwise it aggregates directly.

question: If I change the SQL builder's helper that drops all ORDER BY terms (with a flag that also discards the model's default Meta ordering), which code calls it directly?
expected: Query.clear_ordering is called directly by QuerySet._earliest, QuerySet.delete, QuerySet._combinator_query, QuerySet.order_by (force_empty=False), Query.get_aggregation (inner and outer query), Query.exists, Query.resolve_expression (subquery use), Query.split_exclude and SQLUpdateCompiler.pre_sql_setup.
note: grep 'clear_ordering(' over django/: query.py 662,742,991,1148; sql/query.py 466,506 (get_aggregation),549 (exists),1060 (resolve_expression),1801 (split_exclude); compiler.py 1566 (SQLUpdateCompiler.pre_sql_setup). SCIP misses Query.exists, Query.resolve_expression, SQLUpdateCompiler.pre_sql_setup.

question: If I change the method that walks a list of field names from a starting model, creating or reusing a table alias for every relation hop and returning the final field, target columns and path, which code calls it directly?
expected: Query.setup_joins is called by Query.build_filter (filters), Query.resolve_ref (F()/references), Query.add_fields (values()/only columns), Query.join_parent_model (multi-table inheritance parents), and in the compiler by SQLCompiler._setup_joins (ordering/distinct) and SQLCompiler.get_related_selections (select_related, three call sites).
note: grep '.setup_joins(': compiler.py 774 (_setup_joins), 882/908/947 (get_related_selections); sql/query.py 1035 join_parent_model, 1315 build_filter, 1759 resolve_ref, 1935 add_fields. SCIP misses get_related_selections.

question: When the URL carries no language prefix, Django chooses the visitor's language from the language cookie set by the language-switch view, then from the browser's Accept-Language header (ignoring '*' and malformed tags, falling back from 'de-at' to 'de' if only that is configured), and finally from the site default. Where is this priority order actually implemented?
expected: trans_real.get_language_from_request: optional URL-path check, then the LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME cookie (if in LANGUAGES and check_for_language), then parse_accept_lang_header over HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE with get_supported_language_variant for each entry (break on '*', skip malformed), then settings.LANGUAGE_CODE. The function of the same name in django/utils/translation/__init__.py only delegates to it; LocaleMiddleware.process_request calls it and activates the result.
note: Three defs share the name (trans_real, translation/__init__ delegate, trans_null); only trans_real has the logic.

question: Over HTTPS, a form on https://app.example.com that posts to https://api.example.com gets a 403 saying the referring page does not match any trusted origin, although the token is valid. The same post over plain HTTP works, and setting the anti-forgery cookie domain to '.example.com' makes it pass. Where is this check made, including how a leading-dot entry is matched against subdomains?
expected: CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view, only when request.is_secure(), requires a Referer, rejects malformed or non-https ones, builds good_hosts from CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS plus CSRF_COOKIE_DOMAIN (or SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN with CSRF_USE_SESSIONS, with the port appended) or else request.get_host(), and rejects with REASON_BAD_REFERER unless is_same_domain(referer.netloc, host) holds for one. is_same_domain treats a pattern starting with '.' as matching the domain and all subdomains.

question: My URLs use i18n_patterns. With prefix_default_language=False, a visitor whose browser asks for French and opens /about/ (no prefix) still gets English, while /fr/about/ is French. With prefix_default_language=True, opening /about/ instead sends them a 302 to /fr/about/ (or to /fr/about/ with a slash added). Where is each of these behaviours decided?
expected: LocaleMiddleware.process_request picks the language via get_language_from_request(check_path=...) but forces settings.LANGUAGE_CODE when the path has no language prefix, prefix patterns are used and prefix_default_language is False. LocaleMiddleware.process_response, on a 404 with no language in the path and prefix_default_language True, checks is_valid_path for '/<lang><path>' (or with APPEND_SLASH, the slashed version) and returns response_redirect_class to the prefixed URL.

question: I turned on Django's site-wide page caching (the two-part fetch/update setup). Pages served to first-time visitors who have no cookies yet are never stored once the view touches the session, pages marked private are never stored, and views that set max-age=0 are never stored either. Where is the decision to store or skip the finished page made?
expected: UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response returns without storing when _should_update_cache is false, for streaming or non-200/304 responses, when the request had no cookies but the response sets cookies and has Vary: Cookie (SessionMiddleware adds that), when Cache-Control contains private, or when get_max_age gives 0; otherwise it patches headers, learns the cache key and stores the response.

question: A template prints {{ order.items.0.total }}. Each dotted part is tried as a dictionary key, then as an attribute, then as a list index, and callables are invoked unless they are flagged as not to be called or as altering data. Trace the calls from the compiled template's top-level display entry point (what the Django template backend calls with a context) down to that per-part lookup.
expected: Template.render binds the context and calls Template._render, which calls NodeList.render; that calls Node.render_annotated for each node, which dispatches to VariableNode.render; it calls FilterExpression.resolve, which calls Variable.resolve, which calls Variable._resolve_lookup to walk the dotted lookups (dict, attribute, index; callables, do_not_call_in_templates, alters_data).
note: Edges verified by reading but not SCIP calls: Node.render_annotated -> VariableNode.render (self.render() dispatch; SCIP resolves to Node.render), VariableNode.render -> FilterExpression.resolve (self.filter_expression.resolve, untyped attribute).

question: A client uploads a file whose multipart filename is 'C:\\Users\\me\\evil.txt' or '../../etc/passwd'; my view only sees 'evil.txt' or 'passwd'. Trace the calls from the first access of the uploaded-files mapping on a WSGI-served HTTP call to the code that cleans the client-supplied filename.
expected: WSGIRequest.FILES (lazy property) calls HttpRequest._load_post_and_files, which for multipart/form-data calls HttpRequest.parse_file_upload; that builds a MultiPartParser with the upload handlers and calls MultiPartParser.parse, which for each file part calls sanitize_file_name (html-unescape, strip everything up to the last backslash, os.path.basename).

question: A view ends with Django's one-line shortcut that returns a temporary 302 to a named URL pattern, passing keyword arguments.
