Where is this mapping from a raised error to the status code, logging and page made?
expected: response_for_exception in django/core/handlers/exception.py is the isinstance ladder: Http404 -> technical_404_response under DEBUG or the 404 handler; PermissionDenied -> 403; MultiPartParserError/BadRequest -> 400; SuspiciousOperation -> logs to 'django.security.<ClassName>' and returns technical_500_response(status_code=400) under DEBUG or the 400 handler; SystemExit re-raised; else got_request_exception + handle_uncaught_exception (500). It is called from convert_exception_to_response.inner around every middleware.

question: In a template, {{ event.start|time:"P" }} prints 'midnight' at 00:00, 'noon' at 12:00, '1 a.m.' at 01:00 and '1:30 p.m.' at 13:30: minutes are left off when they are zero and the two special hours get words instead of numbers. Which code produces this one format character's output?
expected: TimeFormat.P in django/utils/dateformat.py: returns _('midnight') for 00:00, _('noon') for 12:00, otherwise '%s %s' % (self.f(), self.a()), where f() drops ':00' minutes and a() gives 'a.m.'/'p.m.'.

question: If I pickle a queryset (for example to put it in the cache), Django runs its SQL first and pickles the fetched rows together with the Django version, but pickling a prefetch_related lookup spec that carries a custom inner queryset does not execute that inner queryset. Where are these two pickling behaviours implemented?
expected: QuerySet.__getstate__ calls self._fetch_all() and returns __dict__ plus DJANGO_VERSION_PICKLE_KEY (QuerySet.__setstate__ warns on version mismatch). Prefetch.__getstate__ replaces its queryset with queryset._chain(_result_cache=[], _prefetch_done=True) so pickling it never hits the database.

question: Two ORM expression objects built separately, e.g. F('price') * 2 written twice, or two Lower('name') calls, compare equal with == and hash the same, so they can be used as dict keys and de-duplicated. The fingerprint is derived from the class plus the arguments the object was constructed with, bound against its constructor signature with defaults filled in, and model fields inside are reduced to (model label, field name). Where is that fingerprint computed?
expected: BaseExpression.identity (a cached_property) binds the stored _constructor_args to inspect.signature(self.__init__), applies defaults, and builds a tuple of the class and (arg, value) pairs, replacing Field instances by (model label, name) and making other values hashable. BaseExpression.__eq__ and __hash__ use it.
note: Read expressions.py BaseExpression.identity/__eq__/__hash__.

question: Reading an upload column on a model instance always gives back an object with .url, .path, .size and .open(), even when the attribute holds a plain path string, None, a raw django File I just assigned, or an object that came back from unpickling without its back-references. Where is the stored value wrapped or repaired into that storage-aware object on attribute access?
expected: FileDescriptor.__get__ (the descriptor of FileField) takes the raw value from instance.__dict__ (via DeferredAttribute.__get__) and wraps str/None in field.attr_class (FieldFile/ImageFieldFile), wraps a bare File in attr_class with _committed=False, restores instance/field/storage on an unpickled FieldFile, and fixes the instance pointer.

question: When new migration files are generated, the first one for an app with no migrations yet is called '0001_initial', and later ones get a number one higher than the leading digits of the app's current latest migration (even if I renamed it, e.g. '0007_custom' gives '0008_...'); each new file also gets a dependency on that latest one, and if I passed --name the given name replaces the automatic suffix. Where are the number, the name and that dependency assigned?
expected: MigrationAutodetector.arrange_for_graph finds the app's current leaf, computes next_number from parse_number(leaf name)+1 (or 1), names each migration '%04i_<name|initial|suggest_name()>', appends the leaf as a dependency of the first new migration, and rewrites dependencies through name_map. It also asks the questioner whether to create an initial migration.

question: I give a DateTimeField a callable default value used when the form is unbound (timezone.now). The rendered input shows the current time without microseconds, but if I use a custom widget that declares it supports microseconds they are kept. Where does the per-field rendering code evaluate that callable and drop the microseconds?
expected: BoundField.initial (a cached_property) asks the form for the field's starting value (BaseForm.get_initial_for_field, which calls a callable), and if the result is a datetime/time and the widget's supports_microseconds is False it replaces microsecond with 0.

question: Setting the password 'jsmith2021' for the account 'jsmith' is refused as too close to the username, and for someone whose address is 'john.smith@example.com' a password resembling just 'smith' is refused as too close to the e-mail address. Which code compares the candidate password with the account's attributes, and how does it split them before comparing?
expected: UserAttributeSimilarityValidator.validate iterates user_attributes (username, first_name, last_name, email by default), splits each string value on non-word characters (re.split(r'\W+')) plus the whole value, and raises ValidationError 'password_too_similar' when SequenceMatcher(...).quick_ratio() of the lowercased strings reaches max_similarity (0.7), naming the field's verbose_name.

question: My site runs behind Apache with mod_rewrite, which rewrites the public URL /shop/cart/ onto the Django entry point. Django still generates links starting with /shop/ because it reconstructs the mount point from the full URL Apache recorded before rewriting, minus the remaining path; if I set FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME, that value wins outright. Where is the mount-point prefix of an incoming request computed from the server's environment?
expected: get_script_name in django/core/handlers/wsgi.py returns settings.FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME if set; otherwise reads SCRIPT_URL or REDIRECT_URL (set by mod_rewrite), collapses repeated slashes, strips PATH_INFO from the end; else falls back to SCRIPT_NAME. It is used by WSGIRequest.__init__ and WSGIHandler.__call__ (which stores it as the thread's script prefix).

question: When Django serializes and signs a Python object with compression requested (as it does for session data and for flash messages kept in a cookie), it runs zlib over the serialized bytes but keeps the compressed form only if it is at least two bytes shorter, then base64-encodes it and puts a leading '.' in front so that the marker itself is covered by the signature, which guards against decompression-bomb payloads. Where is this decided?
expected: Signer.sign_object in django/core/signing.py: serializes, zlib-compresses when compress=True and len(compressed) < len(data) - 1, base64-encodes, prefixes '.', then calls self.sign(). The module-level dumps() only constructs a TimestampSigner and delegates to it; unsign_object is the reverse.

question: filter(id__in=[3, None, 3, 7]) produces SQL with only two placeholders and params [3, 7]: the None and the duplicate are silently dropped, and if nothing is left the queryset comes back empty without hitting the database. Which method strips them?
expected: In.process_rhs (lookups.py): for a direct value it builds an OrderedSet of the rhs and discards None (falling back to a list comprehension for unhashable items), raises EmptyResultSet if nothing is left, then batch_process_rhs builds the '(%s, %s)' placeholder. For a subquery rhs it instead clears the select clause and selects pk if needed.

question: Author.objects.annotate(n=Count('book')) groups by every column of the author table on SQLite, but on PostgreSQL the GROUP BY lists only the author's primary key (and on MySQL only the main table's primary key plus HAVING terms), because those databases accept columns that are functionally dependent on a grouped primary key. Which method shrinks the grouping list this way?
expected: SQLCompiler.collapse_group_by: if features.allows_group_by_pk (MySQL) and the base table's pk is grouped, keeps only that pk, HAVING expressions and columns of tables without a grouped pk; elif features.allows_group_by_selected_pks (PostgreSQL) drops every non-pk column of tables whose pk is in the grouping (skipping unmanaged models via allows_group_by_selected_pks_on_model). It is called from SQLCompiler.get_group_by.
note: Read compiler.py collapse_group_by; features: mysql allows_group_by_pk=True, postgresql allows_group_by_selected_pks=True.

question: With a one-to-one from Restaurant to Place, reading place.restaurant on a place that has no restaurant raises an exception (a subclass of both Restaurant's DoesNotExist and AttributeError) saying the place has no restaurant. The miss is remembered, so reading it again does not hit the database, and on a place that was never written no query is made at all. Where is that access from the side that does not hold the column implemented?
expected: ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.__get__ looks in the related object's cache; on a miss it returns None without a query if instance.pk is None, otherwise queries with get_forward_related_filter and catches DoesNotExist -> None; it caches the result (including None) via self.related.set_cached_value and raises self.RelatedObjectDoesNotExist when the result is None.

question: Running the test suite on SQLite with no TEST NAME configured, every database alias gets its own in-memory test database, and it is still visible to other threads (for example a live-server test), because it is opened as a named shared-cache in-memory URI rather than the plain ':memory:'. Where is that test database name chosen?
expected: The SQLite backend's DatabaseCreation._get_test_db_name returns TEST['NAME'] or ':memory:', and turns ':memory:' into 'file:memorydb_<alias>?mode=memory&cache=shared' so each alias has a distinct shared in-memory database; the base class version would prefix 'test_' to NAME.

question: With USE_TZ = True and the current time zone set to Europe/Paris, a user types '2021-03-28 02:30' into a date-time form input. Instead of a stored value they get a validation message saying the time could not be interpreted in that zone and may be ambiguous or non-existent. Where is a naive submitted value made aware, and where is the DST gap detected?
expected: django/forms/utils.py::from_current_timezone: when USE_TZ and the value is naive it takes the current time zone; for non-pytz zones it checks timezone._datetime_ambiguous_or_imaginary and raises, otherwise make_aware (pytz raises on its own); any exception becomes a ValidationError with code 'ambiguous_timezone'. It is called from DateTimeField.to_python and SplitDateTimeField.compress.

question: Running the management command that gathers static files into STATIC_ROOT a second time reports most files as unmodified and skips them, but if the previous run used --link and this one does not (or the other way round), every file is replaced even though nothing changed. Where is the skip-or-replace decision made for a file that already exists at the destination?
expected: collectstatic's Command.delete_file: if the target exists it compares the target and source modified times (seconds precision); for local storage it only allows skipping when the symlink mode matches (not self.symlink ^ os.path.islink(full_path)); unmodified+skippable files are added to unmodified_files and it returns False, otherwise it deletes the old file (or pretends on dry run) and returns True. copy_file/link_file call it.

question: For a mobile OAuth flow I return a 302 to 'myapp://callback?code=abc'. Instead of sending the browser there, the request ends with a 400 caused by a security-category error complaining about an unsafe protocol, while http, https and ftp targets work. Where is the target URL's scheme checked when Django builds a redirect reply, and how can I allow my scheme?
expected: HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__ (base of HttpResponseRedirect / HttpResponsePermanentRedirect) sets Location via iri_to_uri, parses the URL and raises DisallowedRedirect (a SuspiciousOperation, hence 400) if the scheme is not in the class attribute allowed_schemes = ['http', 'https', 'ftp']. Subclass the redirect class and extend allowed_schemes.

question: With the default flash-message storage, when one request queues so many messages that they no longer fit in the ~4 KB browser-side store, the messages that don't fit are kept server-side in the session instead of being dropped (the newest ones overflow, the oldest stay client-side), and a store that held messages on the previous request is still emptied even when nothing new goes into it. Where is this split between the two stores decided?
expected: FallbackStorage._store in django/contrib/messages/storage/fallback.py: loops over (CookieStorage, SessionStorage), calls each one's _store with remove_oldest=False and passes the unstored remainder to the next; a storage in _used_storages that gets no messages is flushed with _store([], response).

question: My Book model has Meta.ordering = ['title']. Book.objects.first() sorts by title, but Book.objects.values('author').annotate(n=Count('id')).first() sorts by the primary key instead, because Django decides the grouped queryset counts as unsorted. Where is the 'is this queryset sorted?' decision made?
expected: The QuerySet.ordered property: True for EmptyQuerySet, or if extra_order_by/order_by are set, or if default_ordering and Meta.ordering exist and the query has no group_by; a GROUP BY query with only Meta ordering is not considered ordered. QuerySet.first()/last() check it and fall back to order_by('pk') / '-pk'.

question: On Oracle, F('a') % F('b') is emitted as MOD(a, b), .bitand() as BITAND(...), .bitor() is emulated with BITAND and arithmetic, bit shifts become multiplication/division by POWER(2, n), and asking for a bitwise XOR raises NotSupportedError. Which code chooses these Oracle-specific spellings of the arithmetic and bitwise operators?
expected: The Oracle backend's DatabaseOperations.combine_expression maps the connectors ('%%', '&', '|', '<<', '>>', '^', '#') to MOD, BITAND, the BITAND-based OR emulation, POWER-based shifts, POWER, and raises NotSupportedError for XOR; everything else falls through to BaseDatabaseOperations.combine_expression (infix join). CombinedExpression.as_sql calls connection.ops.combine_expression.
note: Read backends/oracle/operations.py combine_expression; each backend overrides the same method name (sqlite, mysql, oracle, base).

question: I assign a Python float such as 1.1 to a fixed-precision numeric column (max_digits=5, decimal_places=2) and run model validation. Instead of the long binary expansion of 1.1 I get a value rounded to the column's total number of digits, while a string like '1.10' is converted exactly and an unparsable string gives an 'invalid' validation error. Where does that conversion of the raw Python value happen?
expected: DecimalField.to_python returns None unchanged, converts a float with self.context.create_decimal_from_float (context = decimal.Context(prec=max_digits)), otherwise decimal.Decimal(value), raising ValidationError code 'invalid' on InvalidOperation/TypeError/ValueError. It is called from Field.clean during clean_fields and from get_prep_value/get_db_prep_save.

question: On SQLite, a data-fixing script wraps a call that alters a table (using the connection's DDL editor in a with-block) inside an outer transaction.atomic() block, and it fails immediately with a 'not supported' error explaining that foreign key checks must be turned off before entering the atomic block, since SQLite cannot switch them off in the middle of a transaction. Where is this refused?
expected: The SQLite DatabaseSchemaEditor.__enter__ calls connection.disable_constraint_checking(); that returns False when inside an atomic block (PRAGMA foreign_keys cannot change mid-transaction), and __enter__ then raises NotSupportedError before delegating to the base __enter__. Its __exit__ re-checks constraints and re-enables checking.

question: In the admin changelist I wrote an action and set allowed_permissions = ('publish',) on it. Staff without that right don't see it in the action dropdown, and Django calls a has_publish_permission method on my admin class to decide. If any one of several listed rights is granted, it shows. Where is that filtering done?
expected: ModelAdmin._filter_actions_by_permissions walks the (callable, name, description) tuples; callables without allowed_permissions pass; otherwise it builds getattr(self, 'has_%s_permission' % p) for each listed permission and keeps the action if any returns True. ModelAdmin.get_actions calls it on the result of _get_base_actions.

question: With the redirects app enabled, a request for /old-page that would 404 is sent on to the new location even though the stored entry is '/old-page/', and an entry whose new path is left blank answers 410 Gone instead of redirecting. Where is that decided?
expected: RedirectFallbackMiddleware.process_response only acts on 404 responses: it looks up a Redirect for the current site and request.get_full_path(), retries with force_append_slash=True when APPEND_SLASH is on and the path lacks a slash, returns response_gone_class (HttpResponseGone) when new_path == '' and response_redirect_class (permanent redirect) otherwise.

question: On the yellow error page and in the admin error e-mails, the table of project configuration shows values such as SECRET_KEY, an API token, or DATABASES['default']['PASSWORD'] as a row of stars. The masking is driven by a case-insensitive pattern over the name, recurses into nested dicts, lists and tuples, and wraps callable values so the page's template will not call them. Where is one configuration name/value pair masked?
expected: SafeExceptionReporterFilter.cleanse_setting(key, value): if hidden_settings (API|TOKEN|KEY|SECRET|PASS|SIGNATURE, re.I) matches the key, returns cleansed_substitute; recurses into dict values (by key) and list/tuple items; wraps callables in CallableSettingWrapper. Called by get_safe_settings (all upper-case settings) and get_safe_request_meta (request.META).

question: A client sends a conditional request header with the obsolete two-digit-year date form, e.g. 'Sunday, 06-Nov-94 08:49:37 GMT'. Django reads it as 1994 rather than 2094, and in general any two-digit year that would land more than 50 years in the future is pushed back a century. Where is such a header date string turned into seconds since the epoch?
expected: parse_http_date in django/utils/http.py: tries the RFC1123, RFC850 and asctime regexes; for year < 100 it adds the current century, or the previous one when the result is more than 50 years ahead; then builds a datetime and returns calendar.timegm(). parse_http_date_safe only wraps it to return None on error.

question: When a relation filter is given a model instance instead of a raw value, e.g. filter(author=some_author) or author__in=[a1, a2], the ORM swaps each instance for the value(s) of the column(s) the foreign key actually targets, walking up parent links when the target field lives on a parent model, falling back to the primary key for a one-to-one primary-key relation, and wraps plain values in a 1-tuple. Which function does that conversion?
expected: get_normalized_value(value, lhs) in fields/related_lookups.py: for a Model instance it takes the path's target_fields, climbs source.remote_field while the instance is not of source.model, collects getattr(value, source.attname) (or returns (value.pk,) on AttributeError); non-tuples become (value,). RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup, RelatedIn.as_sql and RelatedLookupMixin.get_prep_lookup call it.

question: With USE_TZ=True on PostgreSQL I truncate a timestamp to the hour using a fixed-offset tzinfo five hours east of UTC (its name is 'UTC+05:00'). The generated SQL reads ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC-05:00': the sign in the zone name is deliberately inverted, because PostgreSQL reads POSIX-style offset names with the opposite sign convention. Which code flips the sign?
expected: The PostgreSQL backend's DatabaseOperations._prepare_tzname_delta replaces '+' with '-' (and '-' with '+') in the zone name; it is called by DatabaseOperations._convert_field_to_tz, which renders "%s AT TIME ZONE '%s'" when a tzname is given and USE_TZ is on, and which the date/time trunc, extract and cast helpers of that backend call.
note: Read backends/postgresql/operations.py; MySQL has a same-named helper that keeps the sign (strips the 'UTC' prefix), so the backend matters.

question: Model validation rejects a value that is not among a column's declared choices, also looking inside named groups of choices (the nested (group label, [(value, label), ...]) form), and it also produces the 'cannot be null' and 'cannot be blank' errors; columns declared with editable=False are skipped entirely. Where in the model-column layer are these per-value checks done?
expected: Field.validate (model field base class) returns early for non-editable fields, iterates self.choices including optgroups and raises ValidationError('invalid_choice') when no key matches, then raises 'null' when value is None and not null, and 'blank' when not blank and value in empty_values. Field.clean calls it between to_python and run_validators.
note: Subclass overrides (AutoFieldMixin.validate, ArrayField.validate, JSONField.validate) call super or add their own checks; the choices/null/blank logic is only in the base class.

question: On PostgreSQL, a CharField or TextField with db_index=True or unique=True ends up with two indexes: the normal one and a second one using a special operator class, so that LIKE/startswith lookups can use an index when the database collation is not 'C'. Array columns of those types do not get the extra one. Where is the extra index statement built?
expected: postgresql DatabaseSchemaEditor._create_like_index_sql: for db_index/unique fields whose db_type starts with 'varchar' or 'text' (and has no '[' i.e. not an array) it returns _create_index_sql(..., suffix='_like', opclasses=['varchar_pattern_ops'|'text_pattern_ops']); _field_indexes_sql appends it on table creation and _alter_field adds/drops it on changes.

question: Which code computes the CSS/JS asset list of a widget or form class by combining what the class declares in its inner asset-declaration class with what its parent class provides, inheriting everything by default, nothing when the inner class turns inheritance off, and only selected media types when it lists them?
expected: media_property(cls) returns a property whose getter (_media) reads super(cls, self).media as the base, then the class's inner Media definition: extend=True -> base + Media(definition); extend a tuple of media types -> only base[medium] for those; extend False -> Media(definition) alone; no definition -> base. MediaDefiningClass.__new__ installs it.

question: When dumping data with natural foreign keys, Django puts the models in an order where any model whose natural key is referenced (by a foreign key, by a simple auto-created many-to-many, or by an explicit dependencies list declared on the natural key method) comes before the models that reference it; on a cycle it either fails with a 'can't resolve' error or, when cycles are permitted, breaks one arbitrarily. Which function computes that order?
expected: django.core.serializers.sort_dependencies builds (model, deps) pairs from natural_key.dependencies, FK targets with natural_key and auto-created M2M targets, then repeatedly promotes models whose deps are satisfied; with allow_cycles=True it pops the last skipped model, otherwise raises RuntimeError. dumpdata's handle (get_objects) calls it with allow_cycles=True.

question: A URL entry written as path('archive/<int:year>/<slug>/', ...) has to become a regular expression with named groups, where an angle-bracket parameter without a converter defaults to the string converter. Writing '<int: year>' (with a space) or '<int:2year>' or an unregistered converter name makes Django refuse the URL configuration as improperly configured. Where is the angle-bracket syntax translated and validated?
expected: _route_to_regex in django/urls/resolvers.py walks the route with _PATH_PARAMETER_COMPONENT_RE, rejects whitespace inside <...>, non-identifier parameter names and unknown converters (get_converter KeyError) with ImproperlyConfigured, defaults to 'str', escapes literal parts and emits (?P<name>converter.regex); returns the regex and the converters dict. Used by RoutePattern.match/_compile/check.

question: In a view I build label = mark_safe('Total') + ': ' + user_value and print {{ label }}; the tag shows up escaped as <b>. If I instead join two values that were both passed through mark_safe, the result stays unescaped. Where is the rule that decides whether joining two strings keeps the 'safe' marking?
expected: SafeString.__add__ in django/utils/safestring.py: calls str.__add__ and wraps the result in SafeString only if the right-hand operand is SafeData; otherwise it returns a plain str, which autoescaping then escapes.

question: With Book.objects.select_related('editor__country'), each fetched row carries the editor and country columns. For books with no editor I get book.editor == None rather than an Editor full of None fields, and each loaded editor also gets its reverse cache pointing back at the book. Which method, run for every row, decides whether the joined object exists, builds it from its slice of the row, recurses into deeper joined models and wires both caches?
expected: RelatedPopulator.populate(row, from_obj): takes its column slice (or reorder_for_init for parent data), sets obj=None if the pk column is None, else Model.from_db and recurses into its own related_populators; then local_setter(from_obj, obj) and, if obj is not None, remote_setter(obj, from_obj). Created by get_related_populators / RelatedPopulator.__init__, driven from ModelIterable.__iter__.

question: Both qs[5:5] (a slice whose start equals its stop) and the method that hands back a guaranteed-empty queryset give a result that returns no rows without any SQL being sent: the SQL object gets an always-false marker appended to its conditions (and to every sub-statement of a union). Which code calls the helper that appends that marker?
expected: Callers of Query.set_empty (adds NothingNode() with AND, and recurses into combined_queries): QuerySet.none (clone.query.set_empty()) and Query.set_limits (when low_mark == high_mark after clamping). Query.set_empty also calls itself for each combined query. NothingNode.as_sql raises EmptyResultSet, so the compiler returns no rows without executing.
note: grep 'set_empty(' in django/: query.py:921 (QuerySet.none), sql/query.py:1843 (set_empty recursion on combined_queries), 1869 (set_limits). SCIP agrees.

question: The SQL builder for bulk row modification has a method that takes (field, model, value) triples, resolves any value that is an ORM expression against the builder itself (no joins allowed, in for-save mode) and appends them to the list of SET assignments. List every place in Django that calls that method.
expected: UpdateQuery.add_update_fields is called by UpdateQuery.add_update_values (after it has split off parent-model fields and validated the names, the path of QuerySet.update()) and by QuerySet._update (the field-object variant used when an instance is written).
note: grep 'add_update_fields(' over django/: subqueries.py:97 (add_update_values) and query.py:798 (QuerySet._update); SCIP agrees.

question: A model's _meta object keeps many lazily computed properties (field lists, concrete fields, field-name maps, reverse relation lists, the per-argument cache of field listings). One method throws them away, either the forward ones, the reverse ones, or both. Which code calls that method directly? List every caller.
expected: Options._expire_cache is called by Apps.clear_cache (for every model when the registry is ready), Options.add_manager, and Options.add_field (on itself and with forward=False on the related model's _meta when the new field is a relation, else reverse=False).
note: Verified by grep for _expire_cache: 5 call sites in these 3 functions; matches SCIP.

question: When a multi-column uniqueness or multi-column index that was declared in a model's Meta is dropped, the DDL layer has to find the single existing database constraint or index on exactly those columns by introspecting the live database (ignoring ones that are declared by name in Meta.constraints or Meta.indexes), raising an error if it finds zero or more than one, and then drop it. Which code calls this find-and-drop helper? List every caller.
expected: BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor._delete_composed_index is called by alter_unique_together (removed unique_together sets, {'unique': True}, sql_delete_unique), alter_index_together (removed index_together sets, {'index': True, 'unique': False}, sql_delete_index), and the MySQL override _delete_composed_index via super() after recreating an implicit FK index if needed.
note: Completeness: grep '_delete_composed_index(' in django/ gives base schema.py:401, :417 and mysql/schema.py:133 only; matches SCIP callers.

question: The admin escapes primary-key values before putting them in URL paths (a pk with '/' or '_' becomes '_2F' / '_5F'), so links still resolve. Which code calls that escaping helper? List every caller.
expected: admin.utils.quote is called by: AdminReadonlyField.get_admin_url (link to a readonly FK target), LogEntry.get_admin_url (history/recent actions links), ModelAdmin.response_add (popup/obj url after add), the admin_urlquote template filter, the nested format_callback in get_deleted_objects (links on the delete confirmation page), and ChangeList.url_for_result (changelist row links).
note: Grep `quote(` in django/contrib (excluding unquote/urllib) gives exactly these 6 sites; matches SCIP.

question: Django checks a new password against every validator configured in AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS (collecting all their errors into one ValidationError) through a single entry-point function. Which code in Django calls that entry point directly? Include form classes and management commands.
expected: password_validation.validate_password is called by UserCreationForm._post_clean, SetPasswordForm.clean_new_password2 (also used by PasswordChangeForm), AdminPasswordChangeForm.clean_password2, and the changepassword and createsuperuser commands' handle methods.
note: Verified: grep 'validate_password(' over django/ gives exactly these 5 call sites (forms.py:123/349/423, changepassword.py:62, createsuperuser.py:157); key agrees.

question: Under PEP 3333 the WSGI server hands Django every environ value as a native str decoded as ISO-8859-1, which garbles UTF-8 paths and query strings. Django has one small helper that reads a key from the environ and re-encodes it to recover the original bytes. List every function that calls that helper.
expected: get_bytes_from_wsgi(environ, key, default) is called by get_path_info (PATH_INFO), get_script_name (SCRIPT_URL / REDIRECT_URL / PATH_INFO / SCRIPT_NAME), get_str_from_wsgi (which decodes the bytes again, used for HTTP_COOKIE) and the WSGIRequest.GET cached property (QUERY_STRING).
note: Verified by grep 'get_bytes_from_wsgi' over django/: 7 call sites in wsgi.py in these 4 functions; the only other hit is a comment in django/test/client.py.

question: The generic cache backend class has one helper that turns the per-call timeout argument into an absolute expiry time (falling back to the configured default, treating 0 as 'already expired' and None as 'never'). Which methods of Django's built-in backends call this shared version, as opposed to a backend-specific override of it? List every one.
expected: BaseCache.get_backend_timeout is called by DatabaseCache._base_set (set/add/touch all go through it), FileBasedCache._write_content (writes the expiry before the pickled value), LocMemCache._set and LocMemCache.touch. The Memcached backends' calls (add/set/set_many/touch, PyLibMCCache.touch) reach BaseMemcachedCache's override instead; the dummy backend never computes an expiry.
note: Verified by grep of get_backend_timeout over django/: 11 call sites; the 7 in memcached.py resolve to the BaseMemcachedCache override.

question: A many-to-many related manager (author.books, or the prefetch for it) filters through the m2m join table and marks the queryset so that the very next filter() call and the one after it are treated as one filter: they reuse the same join to the intermediate table instead of adding a second one. Which code arms that marker?
expected: Callers of QuerySet._next_is_sticky (sets _sticky_filter=True; QuerySet._chain then sets query.filter_is_sticky so Query.chain keeps used_aliases): ManyRelatedManager._apply_rel_filters (queryset._next_is_sticky().filter(**self.core_filters)) and ManyRelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset (queryset._next_is_sticky().filter(**{'<field>__in': instances})).
note: grep '_next_is_sticky(' in django/: only related_descriptors.py:892 and :915, both inside create_forward_many_to_many_manager.ManyRelatedManager.

question: Oracle and SQLite have no LEFT() string function, so taking the first n characters of a column (and, through inheritance, the last n characters) is rendered there as a SUBSTR(...) call. A small helper builds the equivalent substring expression object for that purpose. Which methods call that helper?
expected: Left.get_substr (Substr(expr, Value(1), length); Right overrides it to Substr(expr, length * -1)) is called by Left.as_oracle and Left.as_sqlite, which Right inherits, so both Left and Right compile through Substr on Oracle and SQLite.
note: grep 'get_substr' over django/: definitions at text.py:134 (Left) and :236 (Right), calls only at text.py:138 and :141; SCIP agrees.

question: A relation may name its target before that model class exists (an 'app_label.ModelName' string, a bare model name, or 'self'). A helper resolves those references relative to the declaring model and schedules a callback to run once all the referenced models are registered. Which code in Django calls that scheduling helper directly? List every caller.
expected: lazy_related_operation is called by RelatedField.contribute_to_class (resolve_related_class), ManyToManyField.contribute_to_class (resolve_through_model), create_many_to_many_intermediary_model (set_managed), ModelBase._prepare (order_with_respect_to accessors) and GenericRelation.contribute_to_class (generic order accessors).
note: Verified by grep for lazy_related_operation: 5 call sites; matches SCIP.

question: Migration steps that drop a named index (or re-create it when the step is reversed) do not carry the index definition themselves: they look it up by its name in the in-memory description of the model taken from the project history before (or after) the step. Which code calls that look-up-index-by-name method? List every caller, including in contrib.
expected: ModelState.get_index_by_name is called by RemoveIndex.database_forwards (from_state model state, then remove_index) and RemoveIndex.database_backwards (to_state, then add_index), and by the PostgreSQL contrib RemoveIndexConcurrently.database_forwards/database_backwards (same with concurrently=True).
note: Completeness: grep 'get_index_by_name(' gives operations/models.py:814,821 and contrib/postgres/operations.py:157,165. The SCIP key misses the two contrib callers (receiver is an untyped state lookup).

question: The admin assembles the raw list of changelist actions for a model admin (the site-wide ones such as delete-selected, then those declared on the class and its parents, de-duplicated by name) before any permission filtering. Which code calls that assembly step? List every caller.
expected: ModelAdmin._get_base_actions is called by ModelAdmin.get_actions (which then filters by permissions) and by two system-check methods: ModelAdminChecks._check_action_permission_methods (admin.E129, has_<perm>_permission exists) and ModelAdminChecks._check_actions_uniqueness (admin.E130, duplicate names).
note: Grep `_get_base_actions(` gives 3 call sites (checks.py:982, 1006; options.py:906); matches SCIP.

question: An e-mail address such as 'Jörg <jörg@exämple.de>' has to be turned into a wire-safe form: the display name encoded as an RFC 2047 header, a non-ASCII local part encoded, the domain converted to punycode, and any embedded newline rejected. Which code calls the helper that does this address formatting directly?
expected: sanitize_address is called by forbid_multi_line_headers (for non-ASCII values of address headers such as To/From/Cc/Reply-To) and by the SMTP EmailBackend._send for the envelope sender and every recipient.
note: Verified: grep 'sanitize_address(' gives message.py:65 (forbid_multi_line_headers) and smtp.py:121-122 (_send); key agrees.

question: When a view raises Http404 or PermissionDenied, or crashes, in production Django renders the project's handler404/handler403/handler500 view, or Django's built-in default when the root URLconf does not define one; the system checks also verify that such custom views accept the right arguments. List every place that asks the root URL configuration object for the view to use for a given status code.
expected: URLResolver.resolve_error_handler(view_type) (reads handlerNNN from the urlconf module or falls back to django.views.defaults / django.conf.urls) is called by get_exception_response (400/403/404 path, then calls callback(request, exception=...)), by handle_uncaught_exception (500 when not DEBUG) and by URLResolver._check_custom_error_handlers (signature check of each handler).
note: Verified by grep 'resolve_error_handler': exactly 3 call sites (exception.py lines 131 and 152, resolvers.py line 423).

question: Django has one lazily evaluated helper object that shortens a string to N characters or N words, appending an ellipsis and optionally keeping markup tags balanced. Which code creates that helper object? List every place, including uses outside the template filters.
expected: django.utils.text.Truncator is constructed by the four template filters truncatechars, truncatechars_html, truncatewords, truncatewords_html; by ForeignKeyRawIdWidget.label_and_url_for_value (admin raw-id label, 14 words); and by the migrate command's Command.describe_operation (shortens the operation description).
note: Verified by grep 'Truncator(' over django/: 6 call sites plus the class definition.

question: The SQL builder keeps a reference count per table alias and a join whose count drops to zero is left out of the FROM clause. Which methods call the helper that decrements an alias's reference count?
expected: Callers of Query.unref_alias: Query.combine (unrefs rhs aliases that were unused there), Query.reset_refcounts (brings counts back to a snapshot), Query.trim_joins (pops trailing joins whose column is available on the previous table), Query.trim_start (drops leading joins of a split_exclude subquery).
note: grep 'unref_alias(' in django/: sql/query.py lines 633 (combine), 849 (reset_refcounts), 1709 (trim_joins), 2317 and 2341 (trim_start); SCIP agrees.

question: On SQLite, date/time truncation, extraction and casting are done by custom SQL functions that Django registers on the connection; each call passes two extra arguments, the active time zone name and the connection's time zone name (or NULL, NULL when time zone support is off). One small helper of the SQLite backend produces that pair of SQL literals. Which methods call it?
expected: sqlite3 DatabaseOperations._convert_tznames_to_sql is called by date_trunc_sql, time_trunc_sql, datetime_cast_date_sql, datetime_cast_time_sql, datetime_extract_sql and datetime_trunc_sql of the same class (time_extract_sql and date_extract_sql do not pass time zones).
note: grep '_convert_tznames_to_sql' over django/: six call sites, all in backends/sqlite3/operations.py; SCIP agrees.

question: Relation descriptors keep the loaded related object in a per-instance cache keyed by the relation's cache name; one mixin method reads it from that cache (raising KeyError or returning a supplied fallback when missing). Which code calls that cache read directly? List every caller.
expected: FieldCacheMixin.get_cached_value is called by ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__get__ (own cache, ancestor link, ancestor's cache), ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__set__ (old related object when setting None), ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.__get__ and __set__ (via self.related, a ForeignObjectRel), and GenericForeignKey.__get__.
note: Verified by grep for get_cached_value: 7 call sites in these 5 functions; matches SCIP.

question: The MIGRATION_MODULES setting lets a project move an app's migrations package elsewhere, or disable migrations for it with None. Which code calls the helper that returns an app's migrations package dotted path (and whether it came from that setting)? List every caller.
expected: MigrationLoader.migrations_module is called by MigrationLoader.load_disk (None -> unmigrated app; import failures handled per explicit flag), MigrationQuestioner.ask_initial (decides whether to create an initial migration from the package contents), and the MigrationWriter.basedir property (directory where new migration files are written; raises if disabled).
note: Completeness: grep 'migrations_module(' gives loader.py:75, questioner.py:38, writer.py:203 only.

question: Django can manufacture a ModelForm class at run time from a model plus fields/exclude/widgets/formfield_callback settings, without anyone writing a class statement. Which code calls that dynamic class builder? List every caller.
expected: forms.models.modelform_factory is called by ModelAdmin.get_form (add/change page form), ModelAdmin.get_changelist_form (list_editable form), modelformset_factory (per-form class of a model formset), and ModelFormMixin.get_form_class in generic CreateView/UpdateView.
note: Grep `modelform_factory(` gives 4 call sites (options.py:710, 778; models.py:884; edit.py:101 via model_forms.modelform_factory); matches SCIP.

question: During dumpdata each object becomes a dict with 'model', 'pk' (left out when natural primary keys are requested and the model defines a natural key) and 'fields'. Which methods call the helper that builds that per-object dict directly?
expected: python.Serializer.get_dump_object is called from the end_object methods of the python serializer (appends to self.objects; pyyaml inherits it), the json serializer (json.dump of the dict, with comma/indent handling) and the jsonl serializer (one dict per line). The GeoJSON serializer overrides get_dump_object rather than calling it.
note: Verified: grep 'get_dump_object(' gives exactly python.py:31, json.py:54, jsonl.py:33 besides the two definitions; key agrees.

question: When an anonymous user hits a login-protected page, Django first turns the current page into a full URL with scheme and host, and only shortens it to a path for the 'next' parameter if the login page has the same scheme and host; the per-site page caching also derives its storage keys from that full URL. List every place in Django's Python code that calls the HttpRequest method producing that absolute URL.
expected: HttpRequest.build_absolute_uri() is called by user_passes_test's inner _wrapped_view (login_required etc.) and AccessMixin.handle_no_permission (LoginRequiredMixin etc.), both then compare scheme/netloc with the login URL; and by _generate_cache_key and _generate_cache_header_key in django/utils/cache.py, which md5 the absolute URL.
note: Verified by grep 'build_absolute_uri' over django/: 4 Python call sites (the other hits are a comment in utils/cache.py and technical_404.html template).

question: For custom template tags declared through the decorator helpers that wrap a plain Python function, one shared function splits the tag's tokens into positional and keyword arguments and checks them against the wrapped function's signature (unexpected keyword, keyword given twice, too many positionals, missing required ones). Which code calls that function? List every place.
expected: parse_bits is called from the nested compile_func inside Library.simple_tag and inside Library.inclusion_tag (the key merges both nested functions into Library.compile_func), and from InclusionAdminNode.__init__ in django/contrib/admin/templatetags/base.py, which the admin's overridable inclusion tags use.
note: Verified by grep 'parse_bits(' over django/: 3 call sites (library.py lines ~119 and ~152, admin/templatetags/base.py ~16). The two nested compile_func closures appear as one symbol in the key.

question: Narrowing Book rows with the everyday keyword-argument method, author__in=Author.objects.exclude(name=''): in the SQL the inner SELECT uses table aliases U0, U1... so they cannot clash with the outer statement's aliases. Trace the calls from that public queryset method to the code that picks the new alias letter and renames the inner statement's tables.
expected: QuerySet.filter -> QuerySet._filter_or_exclude -> QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace -> Query.add_q -> Query._add_q -> Query.build_filter -> Query.resolve_lookup_value (value has resolve_expression) -> QuerySet.resolve_expression -> Query.resolve_expression (clones, marks subquery, clears ordering) -> Query.bump_prefix, which generates the next prefix letter not in subq_aliases and calls Query.change_aliases to rename every alias to '<prefix><n>'.

question: I annotate a moving sum: Sum('amount') over a window ordered by date with a rows-based frame running from 3 rows before the current row to the current row. The SQL contains 'ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW'. Trace the calls from the code that renders the OVER (...) expression to the code that turns the integer -3 into the text '3 PRECEDING'.
expected: Window.as_sql compiles its frame via compiler.compile(self.frame) -> WindowFrame.as_sql, which calls self.window_frame_start_end(connection, start, end); for a rows frame RowRange.window_frame_start_end calls connection.ops.window_frame_rows_start_end, which checks supports_over_clause and calls window_frame_start (negative int -> '%d PRECEDING', 0 -> CURRENT ROW, None -> UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) and window_frame_end. WindowFrame.as_sql fills the template '%(frame_type)s BETWEEN %(start)s AND %(end)s'.
note: SQLCompiler.compile -> WindowFrame.as_sql is a call on an untyped node (as_<vendor> getattr then node.as_sql); WindowFrame.as_sql -> RowRange.window_frame_start_end is an override dispatch (runtime trace). Verified by reading expressions.py and base/operations.py.

question: Inside nested all-or-nothing blocks I register callbacks to run after commit. They do not run when an inner block exits; they run only once the outermost block commits, and callbacks registered inside an inner block that was rolled back to its savepoint are silently dropped. Trace the path from leaving the outermost block to the code that actually invokes the queued callbacks, and name where the dropped ones are discarded.
expected: Atomic.__exit__ commits (connection.commit sets run_commit_hooks_on_set_autocommit_on) and in its finally block, for the outermost block, calls connection.set_autocommit(True); BaseDatabaseWrapper.set_autocommit then calls run_and_clear_commit_hooks, which pops and calls each queued func. Callbacks are queued by BaseDatabaseWrapper.on_commit with the current savepoint ids; BaseDatabaseWrapper.savepoint_rollback removes callbacks whose sids contain the rolled-back savepoint.

question: When I ask a bound ModelForm whether its submitted data is acceptable, the model's own clean() method and its field validators also run, and a ValidationError raised there shows up attached to the right form field. Trace the calls from that acceptability question down to where the model instance validates itself.
expected: BaseForm.is_valid reads the errors property; BaseForm.errors calls full_clean when _errors is None; BaseForm.full_clean runs _clean_fields, _clean_form and then the _post_clean hook, which ModelForm overrides: BaseModelForm._post_clean builds the instance (construct_instance), calls instance.full_clean(exclude=..., validate_unique=False) i.e. Model.full_clean (clean_fields, clean), catches ValidationError and maps it onto form fields via _update_errors, then runs validate_unique.
note: is_valid -> errors is a property read (`self.errors`), real at run time but not a SCIP call. full_clean -> BaseModelForm._post_clean is an override dispatch (runtime_overrides).

question: With the flat pages app hooked in through its fallback class in MIDDLEWARE, a URL that no urlpattern matches is answered with the page stored for that URL instead of the 404: the URL may first be redirected to its trailing-slash form, and anonymous users are sent to the login page when the page requires registration. Trace the calls from the 404 response to the code that renders the stored page.
expected: FlatpageFallbackMiddleware.process_response (only for 404 responses) calls the flatpage view with request.path_info; flatpage looks the page up by URL and current site (get_object_or_404), retries with a trailing slash and returns a permanent redirect when APPEND_SLASH, then calls render_flatpage, which redirects to login when registration_required and the user is anonymous, picks the template, marks title/content safe and renders. Http404 or other errors fall back to the original response.

question: skeleton.html defines {% block content %}, page.html extends it and overrides the block, and detail.html extends page.html and overrides it again; the output shows detail.html's version, and {{ block.super }} inside it shows page.html's. Trace the calls from the point where the child's inheritance tag is executed to the code that picks which level's version of a block is emitted.
expected: ExtendsNode.render fetches the parent (get_parent), creates/reuses a BlockContext in render_context, add_blocks() inserts this template's blocks at the front of each name's FIFO list (and the root's blocks when the parent has no extends), then calls compiled_parent._render -> NodeList.render -> Node.render_annotated -> BlockNode.render, which pops the most-derived block from the BlockContext (BlockContext.pop), renders its nodelist and pushes it back; block.super re-renders with the next one in the list.
note: Node.render_annotated -> BlockNode.render is a runtime-dispatched edge (in runtime_overrides).

question: Book.objects.exclude(author=None) | Book.objects.exclude(editor=None) yields a single SELECT: the right-hand side's joins are merged into the left one (reusing an already-joined table when it can, since this is an OR) and its conditions are rewritten to point at the merged statement's table aliases. Trace the calls from the | operator to the code that rewrites the aliases inside the right-hand conditions.
expected: QuerySet.__or__ (after _merge_sanity_check; a sliced side is first turned into pk__in=values('pk')) -> Query.combine, which asserts same model/not sliced/same distinct, joins each rhs alias via Query.join with reuse, builds change_map, runs JoinPromoter votes, clones rhs.where and calls WhereNode.relabel_aliases(change_map), which walks children and relabels or relabeled_clones each one before adding the tree with OR.

question: With multi-table inheritance (Restaurant inherits from Place, 'name' lives on Place), Restaurant.objects.filter(serves_pizza=True) followed by the queryset method that issues a SQL UPDATE with name='X' and serves_pizza=False runs an UPDATE on the restaurant table and then a second UPDATE on the place table, limited to the primary keys that were selected beforehand. Trace from the public queryset method to the code that produces the extra UPDATE for the parent table, and name where parent-table assignments are set aside when the keyword arguments are processed.
expected: QuerySet.update chains to an UpdateQuery and calls UpdateQuery.add_update_values, which for each field whose concrete model is not the queryset's model calls add_related_update (stored per ancestor in related_updates) and passes the rest to add_update_fields. Executing the compiler (SQLUpdateCompiler.execute_sql) runs the main UPDATE, then iterates self.query.get_related_updates(), which builds one UpdateQuery per ancestor model filtered on pk__in related_ids, and executes each. SQLUpdateCompiler.pre_sql_setup pre-selects the ids (related_ids) because related updates exist.
note: QuerySet.update -> SQLUpdateCompiler.execute_sql goes through query.get_compiler (compiler class looked up by name); the key has the edge from the runtime trace. Other leg: QuerySet.update -> UpdateQuery.add_update_values -> UpdateQuery.add_related_update (direct calls).

question: I load rows with .only('title') and later read another column on one of the instances. Django then runs one extra query that fetches just that column for that one row and stores it on the instance (except when the missing column is the child's primary key under multi-table inheritance, which it reads from the parent link instead). Trace the calls from the attribute read to the code that issues the reload and works out which columns are still missing.
expected: Each concrete column is a DeferredAttribute descriptor. DeferredAttribute.__get__ finds the attname missing from instance.__dict__, tries _check_parent_chain (pk via ancestor link), else calls instance.refresh_from_db(fields=[attname]). Model.refresh_from_db builds a _base_manager query with .only(fields), uses get_deferred_fields() to know what is not loaded, copies loaded values and clears cached relations.

question: I add a non-nullable column without a default to an existing model and generate migration files interactively. I'm offered two options (give a one-off value now, or quit and edit the model), and if I choose the first I can type a Python expression such as timezone.now, which is evaluated with the datetime and timezone modules available. Trace the calls from the management command's handler to the code that evaluates what I typed.
expected: makemigrations Command.handle -> MigrationAutodetector.changes -> _detect_changes -> generate_added_fields -> _generate_added_field, which computes preserve_default (null, has_default, M2M, blank text, auto_now) and otherwise asks self.questioner.ask_not_null_addition (or ask_auto_now_add_addition); InteractiveMigrationQuestioner.ask_not_null_addition shows the two-choice menu and calls _ask_default, which loops on input() and eval()s the code with {'datetime', 'timezone'}. The AddField gets preserve_default=False.
note: _generate_added_field -> InteractiveMigrationQuestioner.ask_not_null_addition is a runtime-dispatched edge (self.questioner is typed as the base MigrationQuestioner); it is in runtime_overrides.

question: On an admin changelist I click 'Yes' under the sidebar filter for a boolean column, so the URL gets ?is_active__exact=1 and the list shrinks. Trace from the changelist page view to the code that actually narrows the database query with that selection.
expected: ModelAdmin.changelist_view calls get_changelist_instance, which instantiates the ChangeList; ChangeList.__init__ computes self.queryset = self.get_queryset(request); ChangeList.get_queryset builds filter specs via get_filters (FieldListFilter.create -> BooleanFieldListFilter, whose FieldListFilter.__init__ moves matching GET params into used_parameters) and then calls each spec's queryset(request, qs); FieldListFilter.queryset does queryset.filter(**self.used_parameters).
note: get_changelist_instance -> ChangeList.__init__ is a constructor call (`ChangeList(...)` from self.get_changelist()); the key records it as a call to the class, not to __init__. Real at run time.

question: When I start the development server with --noreload it runs the system checks, warns about unapplied migrations, prints the 'Starting development server at ...' banner and then loads the WSGI application named by the WSGI_APPLICATION setting. Trace from the command's entry point to the function that reads that setting.
expected: runserver Command.handle parses addr/port and calls Command.run, which (without the reloader) calls Command.inner_run directly; inner_run runs self.check, check_migrations, writes the banner, then self.get_handler, whose base implementation returns basehttp.get_internal_wsgi_application(), which imports settings.WSGI_APPLICATION (falling back to get_wsgi_application when unset); inner_run then calls basehttp.run. With staticfiles installed, its runserver Command.get_handler overrides get_handler and wraps the handler in StaticFilesHandler.

question: With SESSION_ENGINE set to keep the whole session inside the browser cookie, a user who edits the cookie value, or whose cookie is older than SESSION_COOKIE_AGE, silently gets an empty fresh session instead of an error. Trace the calls from the first lazy read of the session data to the hash comparison that rejects the edited value.
expected: SessionBase._get_session calls self.load(), i.e. signed_cookies SessionStore.load, which calls signing.loads(session_key, max_age=get_session_cookie_age(), salt=...) -> TimestampSigner.unsign_object (Signer.unsign_object) -> TimestampSigner.unsign (checks the age against max_age, raising SignatureExpired) -> Signer.unsign, which compares the signature with constant_time_compare and raises BadSignature. load() catches any exception, calls self.create() and returns {}.
note: _get_session -> signed_cookies SessionStore.load and Signer.unsign_object -> TimestampSigner.unsign are runtime-dispatched edges (in runtime_overrides).

question: Category.objects.get(parent=None) compiles to parent_id IS NULL, while Product.objects.get(price__gt=None) raises ValueError saying None cannot be used as a value to compare against. Trace the calls from get() to the method that makes that choice.
expected: QuerySet.get -> QuerySet.filter -> QuerySet._filter_or_exclude -> QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace -> Query.add_q -> Query._add_q -> Query.build_filter -> Query.build_lookup, which instantiates the lookup and, if lookup.rhs is None and the lookup cannot take None, raises ValueError unless the lookup is exact/iexact, in which case it returns the field's isnull lookup with True (it does the same for '' on backends that treat empty strings as NULL).

question: Author.objects.annotate(newest=Subquery(Book.objects.filter(author=OuterRef('pk')).order_by('-pub_date').values('title')[:1])). When the inner queryset is built, OuterRef('pk') is replaced by a placeholder that still only knows the name 'pk'; it becomes a real column of the author table only once the outer queryset takes in the annotation. Trace the calls from the outer queryset registering the annotation to the point at which that placeholder is looked up by name against the outer model.
expected: Query.add_annotation resolves the Subquery (BaseExpression.resolve_expression on its source, the inner Query) -> Query.resolve_expression clones the inner query, bumps its alias prefix and resolves its WHERE tree: WhereNode.resolve_expression -> WhereNode._resolve_node walks children and lookups -> WhereNode._resolve_leaf resolves the lookup's rhs, which is the ResolvedOuterRef created earlier by OuterRef.resolve_expression; ResolvedOuterRef.resolve_expression calls F.resolve_expression, i.e. outer_query.resolve_ref('pk'), returning a Col on the outer table alias, and marks possibly_multivalued if the name contains '__'.
note: _resolve_leaf -> ResolvedOuterRef.resolve_expression and BaseExpression.resolve_expression -> Query.resolve_expression are calls on untyped receivers; verified by reading where.py, query.py and expressions.py.

question: When I declare title = models.CharField(max_length=100) in a model class body, by the time the class exists the column has its attname and db column computed and sits in the class's ordered list of local columns (in declaration order, with the primary key set up if it is one). Trace the calls from model class creation to the code that inserts the column into that ordered list.
expected: ModelBase.__new__ calls new_class.add_to_class(name, value) for every attribute with contribute_to_class; ModelBase.add_to_class calls value.contribute_to_class(cls, name); Field.contribute_to_class calls set_attributes_from_name (attname, column) and cls._meta.add_field(self), which bisect.insort's it into local_fields by creation_counter, calls setup_pk and expires caches.

question: When a migration that creates a brand-new table is applied, the CREATE TABLE statement is executed right away, but the table's single-column and Meta indexes, its multi-column uniqueness, and (on backends that cannot declare foreign keys inline in the column definition) its foreign key constraints are only queued and executed when the DDL editor's with-block finishes without an error. Trace from the migration step that creates the table to where a foreign key constraint statement gets queued, and name where the queued statements are finally run.
expected: CreateModel.database_forwards -> schema_editor.create_model -> table_sql, which builds column definitions, appends unique_together statements (_create_unique_sql) and, when sql_create_inline_fk is not set and the backend supports FKs, _create_fk_sql(...) to self.deferred_sql; create_model executes the CREATE TABLE and extends deferred_sql with _model_indexes_sql (field indexes, index_together, Meta.indexes), then recurses for auto-created M2M through tables. BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.__exit__ executes every deferred statement when no exception occurred (then closes the atomic block).
note: CreateModel.database_forwards -> create_model is in the key even though schema_editor is a parameter.

question: The admin change page for an Author shows a tabular inline of Books. Trace how the inline's formset class is manufactured on that page: from the change page view down to the generic function that finally creates the formset class.
expected: ModelAdmin.change_view -> changeform_view -> _changeform_view -> _create_formsets -> get_formsets_with_inlines (yields inline.get_formset(request, obj) per inline instance) -> InlineModelAdmin.get_formset (fields/exclude/readonly, extra/min/max, can_delete, DeleteProtectedModelForm) -> inlineformset_factory (finds the FK) -> modelformset_factory (builds the form via modelform_factory) -> formset_factory (creates the FormSet class with type()).

question: The admin's 'View on site' button points at /admin/r/<content type id>/<object id>/, which redirects to something like http://example.com/articles/34/. When the object's absolute URL is only a path and the object has no relation to a Site, where does the domain come from (SITE_ID is set)? Trace from the redirect view to the lookup of the domain.
expected: contenttypes.views.shortcut loads the object via the ContentType, calls get_absolute_url, returns it unchanged if it is already absolute, otherwise takes get_current_site(request).domain, then overrides it with a Site found through an M2M or FK to Site on the object; get_current_site calls Site.objects.get_current(request) (RequestSite when sites isn't installed), and SiteManager.get_current uses settings.SITE_ID via _get_site_by_id (cached in SITE_CACHE). The redirect is '<request.scheme>://<domain><path>'.

question: A view returns a TemplateResponse with request=request and a dict that contains 'user'. question: An app has 0001..0004 applied and I run the management command that applies migrations with that app's label and '0002' as the target. question: With DEBUG on, the yellow error page shows seven lines of source around every frame, for the raised error and for each error it was chained from, and it still shows source for modules imported from a zip file by asking the module's loader. question: With ATOMIC_REQUESTS=True, if my function view raises after writing rows, the writes are rolled back. question: My project is mounted at /shop under gunicorn (the server passes SCRIPT_NAME=/shop). Inside views, reverse('cart') returns '/shop/cart/'. question: In my own profile view I call set_password() on request.user and then persist the user. Their callers: PermissionsMixin.has_perms and AnonymousUser.has_perms, the {{ perms }} template proxy PermLookupDict.__getitem__, and the admin's BaseModelAdmin.has_add/change/delete/view_permission and InlineModelAdmin._has_any_perms_for_target_model (via request.user.has_perm). permission_required and PermissionRequiredMixin go through has_perms, so they are a third level.
note: Verified: grep '_user_has_perm(' -> models.py:300,452; grep 'has_perm(' (non-def) -> models.py:307,455, context_processors.py:13, admin/options.py:483,498,513,530-531,2162 (autocomplete.py:22 is its own has_perm, backends.py are backend methods). Matches key depth 2.

question: Error reports hide values that views marked as sensitive (POST fields, local variables) only in production; with DEBUG on everything is shown. If I change the per-hit switch that decides whether this masking applies, which code depends on it directly or within two levels of callers?
expected: SafeExceptionReporterFilter.is_active (returns settings.DEBUG is False) is called by get_cleansed_multivaluedict, get_post_parameters and get_traceback_frame_variables (level 1). Level 2: cleanse_special_types (calls get_cleansed_multivaluedict), ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_data (filter.get_post_parameters) and ExceptionReporter.get_exception_traceback_frames (filter.get_traceback_frame_variables).
note: Verified by grep '.is_active(' (3 sites, debug.py 149/165/215) and grep of each level-1 name (get_cleansed_multivaluedict: debug.py 192; get_post_parameters: 317; get_traceback_frame_variables: 482). No other callers in django/.

question: If I change the function that returns a locale-aware format setting for the active language (DATE_INPUT_FORMATS, DECIMAL_SEPARATOR, NUMBER_GROUPING and so on), looking in the locale's format modules before falling back to settings and caching the result per language, which functions call it directly?
expected: get_format (django/utils/formats.py) is called directly by date_format, time_format, number_format, localize_input and sanitize_separators in the same module; by DateTimeFormatsIterator.__iter__ (DateTimeField input formats); by DateTimeBaseInput.format_value and SelectDateWidget._parse_date_fmt / format_value / value_from_datadict; and by views.i18n.get_formats (the JavaScript catalog's format table).

question: If I change the generic (non-SQLite) implementation that derives the connection settings, in particular the database name with a numeric suffix, of the n-th parallel test database clone, which functions call it directly and would see the change? Leave out code that, on its backend, actually reaches an override.
expected: BaseDatabaseCreation.get_test_db_clone_settings ('<NAME>_<suffix>') is called by BaseDatabaseCreation.destroy_test_db (when a suffix is given), the MySQL and PostgreSQL DatabaseCreation._clone_test_db (target name of the clone), and django.test.runner._init_worker (each parallel worker switches connection.settings_dict to its clone). The SQLite _clone_test_db calls the SQLite override instead (file name '<root>_<suffix>.<ext>' or the same in-memory settings), so it is not affected; Oracle does not support cloning here.
note: Completeness: grep 'get_test_db_clone_settings(' gives base/creation.py:268, sqlite3/creation.py:62 (reaches the SQLite override), mysql/creation.py:34, postgresql/creation.py:59, test/runner.py:329. _init_worker uses connection.creation (untyped receiver), so SCIP may miss it.

question: When a list of migration steps is being merged into fewer steps, a step can be combined with a later one even when unrelated steps sit between them. If the combination is allowed, the merged result is normally placed after the in-between steps; but if an earlier in-between step refused to let the first one move past it, the merged result is placed before the in-between steps only if every in-between step can itself be moved across the later step; otherwise the first step is kept as is. The whole pass is repeated until nothing changes. Where is the in-between placement decided?
expected: MigrationOptimizer.optimize_inner compares each operation with every later one via operation.reduce(other); on a list result it does a right reduction (in_between + result) if right is still True, else a left reduction (result + in_between) only when all(op.reduce(other) is True for op in in_between); a falsy reduce result sets right=False. MigrationOptimizer.optimize loops optimize_inner until stable.
note: Operation.reduce overrides (CreateModel.reduce etc.) decide whether a pair combines; the placement logic is only in optimize_inner.

question: Behind gunicorn, every ordinary HTML page my project serves carries a Content-Length header although none of my views set one, while streaming replies do not get it; on a project started from a bare settings file with an empty MIDDLEWARE it is missing. Which code adds that header?
expected: CommonMiddleware.process_response: after the APPEND_SLASH 404 redirect check, it sets response.headers['Content-Length'] = len(response.content) for non-streaming responses that lack the header. Distractors: GZipMiddleware only sets it after compressing, FileResponse.set_headers only for file-like objects, runserver's ServerHandler is not gunicorn, RedirectView.options sets '0'.

question: On SQLite, a computed value whose result type is a DecimalField (an arithmetic combination or an SQL function call) gets wrapped in CAST(... AS NUMERIC) so that comparisons work. For a running total over a window of a decimal column, however, the cast must go around the entire 'SUM(...) OVER (...)' rather than inside the OVER clause, so the inner aggregate is temporarily told to produce a float. Which code makes sure the cast ends up outside the window rather than inside it?
expected: SQLiteNumericMixin.as_sqlite (mixed into Func, CombinedExpression and Window) compiles via as_sql and wraps the SQL in CAST(%s AS NUMERIC) when output_field is a DecimalField. Window.as_sqlite copies the window, sets the source expression's output_field to FloatField so the inner aggregate is not cast, and calls SQLiteNumericMixin.as_sqlite on the copy (super(Window, copy).as_sqlite) so the cast wraps the whole window expression.
note: Many as_sqlite overrides exist (functions/*, ExpressionList, Func-derived); read expressions.py SQLiteNumericMixin and Window.

question: For a reverse foreign key or many-to-many manager (author.books.all()), the manager's own 'belongs to this author' filter is not compiled into the SQL object when the related queryset is created: it is parked on the new clone and only applied the first time anything reads the queryset's underlying SQL object, which saves work when that queryset is thrown away or replaced (e.g. by a prefetch cache). Where is the filter postponed, and where is it finally applied?
expected: Related managers' _apply_rel_filters set queryset._defer_next_filter = True before calling filter(). QuerySet._filter_or_exclude sees the flag, resets it and stores (negate, args, kwargs) in clone._deferred_filter instead of calling _filter_or_exclude_inplace. The QuerySet.query property getter applies the parked filter via _filter_or_exclude_inplace the first time .query is read, then clears _deferred_filter.
note: QuerySet.query is a property getter; SCIP records the getter as query.py::QuerySet.query.

question: When Django lists all columns and relations of a model, it recurses into parent classes, makes sure a diamond-shaped inheritance hierarchy does not contribute the same parent twice, drops grandparents' parent-link one-to-ones that do not belong to this concrete class, can restrict the walk to proxy parents only, adds relations pointing at the model only for non-proxy models (optionally including hidden ones), adds generic/private columns only at the outermost call, and memoizes the result per combination of arguments. Where is that walk implemented?
expected: Options._get_fields(forward, reverse, include_parents, include_hidden, seen_models) does all of this: seen_models for diamonds, PROXY_PARENTS filtering, parent_link filter, _relation_tree for reverse fields unless proxy, private_fields only when topmost_call, and _get_fields_cache keyed by the arguments. Options.get_fields is a thin public wrapper.

question: If I open an admin change URL with a malformed id (e.g. /admin/shop/order/not-a-uuid/change/ for a UUID primary key, or an integer pk that doesn't exist), I get neither a 500 nor a 404: I'm redirected to the admin index with a warning that the item may have been deleted. Where is the malformed id swallowed so that this happens?
expected: ModelAdmin.get_object converts the URL value with field.to_python and fetches it, catching DoesNotExist, ValidationError and ValueError and returning None; the change/delete/history views then call _get_obj_does_not_exist_redirect, which adds the warning message and redirects to admin:index.

question: In a syndication feed class each piece of metadata (title, link, item_description, item_pubdate, ...) can be given as a plain class attribute, as a method taking no arguments, or as a method taking the object or item. Django tells the last two apart without calling the method and catching TypeError, by inspecting the function's argument count. Where?
expected: Feed._get_dynamic_attr(attname, obj, default) in contrib/syndication/views.py: getattr with default on AttributeError; if callable, reads attr.__code__ (or attr.__call__.__code__) and calls attr(obj) when co_argcount == 2 (self + one arg), else attr(); non-callables are returned as is. get_feed, item_link/item_title/item_description and friends go through it.

question: The built-in tag pair that outputs its body exactly as written (handy for showing {{ }} syntax meant for a client-side JS framework) keeps everything between the opening and the closing tag as literal text, and you can name the pair so that the body may itself contain a plain closing tag. While the template source is being split into pieces, where is the decision made to treat tag-looking chunks as plain text until the matching closing tag appears?
expected: Lexer.create_token in django/template/base.py: when a block token's content starts with 'verbatim' it records self.verbatim = 'end' + content; while self.verbatim is set every chunk (tags, variables, comments) becomes a TEXT token, until a block token whose content equals that stored end-tag string clears it. Both Lexer.tokenize and DebugLexer.tokenize go through it; the VerbatimNode in defaulttags only outputs the already-literal content.
